title: AI Engineering & Generative AI
tagline: From AI Fundamentals to Production-Ready Applications
headline: Don't Just Use AI. Learn to Engineer It.
supportingText: Learn to build intelligent applications using Generative AI, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, AI agents, and modern deployment practices—with guidance from experienced industry practitioners.
learningFormat: Live instructor-led sessions, hands-on coding labs, guided projects, and a capstone
instructorProfile: Industry practitioners with at least 4 years of relevant experience
courseLevel: Beginner to Intermediate, with programming fundamentals covered at the beginning

differentiators.title: Learn from industry practitioners

differentiators.description: Progress systematically from Python foundations and LLM API integrations through advanced RAG architectures, multi-agent workflows, evaluation, and cloud deployment.

audienceTracks.title: For College Students & Aspiring Engineers
audienceTracks.description: Bridge the academic gap with cutting-edge industry practices. Build demonstrable software projects to distinguish your resume for software engineering and AI-oriented careers.
benefits: Strengthen your personal portfolio with deployable AI applications
Master foundational Python and clean programming standards before complex AI topics
Learn how real engineering teams evaluate, secure, and ship software
Prepare for modern technology roles with practical, verifiable skills

audienceTracks.title: For Working Professionals & Developers
audienceTracks.description: Upskill into applied Generative AI and LLM systems. Gain the architecture and implementation know-how required to design and deploy AI features in your current or future organization.
benefits: Master RAG architectures, embeddings, and vector databases for internal knowledge bases
Design autonomous AI agents and controlled tool-calling workflows
Integrate AI features seamlessly with backend APIs, authentication, and frontends
Optimize operational token costs, monitoring, logging, and production reliability

learningObjectives: Master Python syntax, functional patterns, and modular project organization
Configure virtual environments and manage dependencies reliably
Handle JSON serialization, API requests, and asynchronous primitives
importantConcepts: Python data structures (lists, dicts, tuples, sets)
Virtual environments (venv/pip) and packaging
JSON manipulation and RESTful HTTP API consumption
Asyncio basics for high-throughput AI API calls
handsOnActivities: Build an API client utility to fetch, parse, and transform nested JSON datasets
Implement an asynchronous batch worker script to process multi-item requests
expectedOutcomes: Write clean, idiomatic Python code suited for downstream AI framework integrations

learningObjectives: Understand the core distinctions between symbolic AI, ML, and deep learning
Differentiate supervised, unsupervised, and self-supervised paradigms
Comprehend model training, loss functions, and evaluation metrics
importantConcepts: Features, labels, training datasets, and validation splits
Classification vs. regression vs. generative tasks
Evaluation metrics: Precision, Recall, F1, Accuracy, and Confusion Matrices
The life cycle of machine learning models from training to inference
handsOnActivities: Train and evaluate a baseline tabular classifier using a standard ML dataset
Perform exploratory data analysis and visualize feature correlations
expectedOutcomes: Articulate the fundamental mechanics of ML systems and model performance evaluation

curriculum.topic: Deep Learning and Neural Network Fundamentals
learningObjectives: Grasp how multi-layer perceptrons process multi-dimensional data
Understand embeddings and high-dimensional semantic vector spaces
Understand the Transformer architecture conceptually (self-attention mechanism)
importantConcepts: Neurons, activation functions, forward propagation, and backpropagation
Dense vectors and cosine similarity in semantic spaces
Tokens, vocabulary tokenization (BPE), and context window boundaries
Transformer encoder-decoder vs. decoder-only architectures
handsOnActivities: Calculate and visualize semantic similarity across word and sentence embeddings
Inspect tokenization behavior across diverse text inputs and languages
expectedOutcomes: Explain how modern foundation models represent language and interpret context limits

learningObjectives: Design precise, deterministic system and user prompts for production tasks
Apply few-shot learning and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) techniques
Enforce structured JSON outputs and validate them against strict schemas
importantConcepts: Role definition, delimiters, and clear instruction formulation
Few-shot exemplars and task demonstration
JSON mode and JSON schema validation (Pydantic / Zod principles)
Prompt regression testing and failure mode taxonomy
handsOnActivities: Build a multi-step structured data extraction pipeline that validates outputs against schemas
Create an automated test suite comparing output consistency across prompt revisions
expectedOutcomes: Reliably extract, validate, and format LLM responses into structured data for software systems

learningObjectives: Connect software applications to leading commercial and open LLM APIs
Handle streaming responses via Server-Sent Events (SSE) for low perceived latency
Manage conversation state, token budgets, and graceful error handling
importantConcepts: API authentication, environment variables, and client initialization
Streaming chunk processing and token generators
Conversation history management and context window truncation strategies
Rate limiting, exponential backoff retries, and token accounting
handsOnActivities: Build a streaming multi-turn chat interface with session history memory
Implement a robust API wrapper with automatic retry policies and token usage logging
expectedOutcomes: Develop responsive, stateful conversational applications powered by LLM endpoints

learningObjectives: Understand why RAG is essential to prevent hallucinations and access private data
Implement document parsing, chunking, and embedding pipelines
Query vector databases and synthesize grounded responses with citations
importantConcepts: Text extraction (PDFs, Markdown, HTML) and preprocessing
Chunking strategies: fixed size, sliding window, and semantic boundary chunking
Vector search: k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN), Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN), and HNSW
Context synthesis, prompt stuffing, source citation, and retrieval grounding
handsOnActivities: Build an end-to-end document question-answering application over multi-page PDF documents
Experiment with chunk size variations and benchmark retrieval precision on real queries
expectedOutcomes: Architect and implement production-ready RAG workflows connecting LLMs to external documents

learningObjectives: Understand autonomous agent architecture and ReAct (Reason + Act) loops
Configure models to call external tools, APIs, and computational functions
Incorporate state management, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop approvals
importantConcepts: Function/tool calling definitions and tool execution loops
Multi-step reasoning and dynamic planning
Stateful agent orchestration and memory checkpoints
Security boundaries, permissions, and human approval gates for critical actions
handsOnActivities: Build a controlled AI assistant capable of searching documentation, running calculations, and querying an API
Implement a human-in-the-loop confirmation gate before executing state-changing operations
expectedOutcomes: Build deterministic, reliable AI agents that safely interface with external software tools

learningObjectives: Design production RESTful API endpoints for asynchronous AI services
Connect an AI backend service to a clean, responsive web user interface
Implement authentication, session isolation, and input validation
importantConcepts: FastAPI / Express API design for AI workloads
CORS, authentication tokens, and user session management
Request sanitization and schema validation
WebSocket vs. Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming to modern frontend clients
handsOnActivities: Develop a complete full-stack web interface connected to an AI backend pipeline
Implement real-time token streaming and status loaders in the UI
expectedOutcomes: Bridge AI backend functionality with user-facing interfaces into a coherent web product

learningObjectives: Systematically evaluate generated answers for groundedness, relevance, and safety
Detect and prevent prompt injection, jailbreaks, and sensitive data leakage
Establish automated test datasets and evaluation benchmarks
importantConcepts: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation frameworks and automated rubrics
Groundedness, faithfulness, and answer relevance scoring
Security threats: Direct prompt injection, indirect prompt injection, and PII leakage
Input/output guardrails and content moderation filters
handsOnActivities: Build an evaluation suite that tests a RAG pipeline against a golden question-answer dataset
Implement defensive input sanitization and guardrail checks to block prompt injection attempts
expectedOutcomes: Apply testing, security hardening, and objective evaluation to AI applications

learningObjectives: Containerize AI applications with Docker and configure environment secrets
Deploy applications to cloud platforms with observability and health checks
Monitor latency, error rates, and optimize operational token expenditure
importantConcepts: Docker containerization, multi-stage builds, and environment configuration
Application telemetry, logging, structured tracing, and request IDs
Token usage tracking, caching strategies, and smaller model distillation trade-offs
Pre-deployment checklists and production readiness reviews
handsOnActivities: Containerize an AI backend and deploy it to a live cloud host
Configure centralized logging and calculate estimated token costs under varying query volumes
expectedOutcomes: Deploy, monitor, and cost-optimize live AI applications for production reliability

learningObjectives: Select and scope an end-to-end real-world industry problem
Design the complete system architecture incorporating RAG, tools, or agents
Build, test, deploy, and document a working, portfolio-ready application
importantConcepts: System architecture specification and component trade-offs
Integration of all program modules into a unified product
Documentation, README architecture diagrams, and demonstration preparation
Peer review and constructive architectural critique
handsOnActivities: Execute the end-to-end development of an approved capstone project
Present the live application, explain architectural choices, and deliver documentation
expectedOutcomes: Demonstrate practical competence through a deployed, fully documented AI software system

faqs.q: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes. The course is designed for beginner to intermediate learners. It begins with Module 1 covering Python for AI Engineering, ensuring learners have the required programming fundamentals before advancing to machine learning, LLMs, and RAG architectures.

Yes. The 72-hour planned learning curriculum is structured over an 8-week schedule with live online sessions designed to accommodate the schedules of working developers and full-time college students.

faqs.q: What is the tuition fee and payment options?
faqs.a: The early-bird admission fee is ₹19,999 (save ₹10,000 from standard ₹29,999). It covers the complete 72 hours of live instruction, 11 modules, hands-on labs, 4 projects, milestone capstone reviews, and verified certificate.
Yes, the program is 100% online. It features live instructor-led sessions, cloud-based coding laboratories, and online capstone reviews.

faqs.q: Do I need an expensive GPU or special hardware?
faqs.a: No expensive local GPU is required. The program leverages cloud-hosted LLM endpoints, lightweight Python environments, and browser-accessible development environments.

faqs.q: Will I build a real-world project for my portfolio?
faqs.a: Yes. Beyond coding exercises in every module, you will design, build, test, and deploy an end-to-end Capstone Project that can be presented in your professional GitHub portfolio.
All sessions are led by industry practitioners with at least 4 years of relevant software engineering and production AI experience.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss a live session?
faqs.a: All live sessions are recorded and provided to enrolled cohort participants for review and study throughout the program.
